phrase.text: A value only moves by itself from one type to another when the target type contains it whole: from
and from a subclass to its superclass.

runs.text: A value only moves by itself from one type to another when the target type contains it whole: from
and from a subclass to its superclass.
Two types can be related in three different ways, and they should not be mixed up:

entries.text: : a value of one fits into the other without losing anything.
: a value can be stored in a variable of the other, either because they are equal or because it widens.

runs.text: There are three widenings, and no more:

blocks.description: Three green arrows: from Integer to Real, from Character to String and from a subclass to its superclass. Below, in red, the conversions that never happen by themselves: Real to Integer, Boolean to number and number to text.

caption.text: The only three arrows the engine follows on its own. The crossed-out arrows require a conversion function.

runs.text: Widening applies when initialising, assigning, passing an argument by value, returning a result and storing in a collection. Also when comparing: a character compared with a string is widened to a string before comparing.

blocks.title: Automatic widenings

runs.text: In the opposite direction there is no widening: a
is not a number and a number does not turn into text by itself.

blocks.title: An integer is not a text

diagnostics.message: Incompatible types in assignment: cannot assign Entero to Cadena

runs.text: By-reference parameters are the exception: they require exactly the same type, without widening, because the subroutine will write to the original variable.

points.text: Equality, widening and assignability are different relations.
Everything else is requested with a conversion function.
By reference requires the exact type.
